clue.text: Could be the duchess's make-up?

parts.note: the duchess is a stage role, such as Webster's Duchess of Malfi, and the actor playing her wears theatrical cosmetics

explanation.surface: A guess at what cosmetics an aristocratic lady might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The duchess seems to be a real noblewoman; she is a part in a play, so her make-up is the theatre kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage actors apply this thick theatrical cosmetic before performing a role.

clue.text: Fish eggs that got higher, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: something that got higher rose

explanation.surface: Fish spawn that somehow climbed upwards, so rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard roe is the mass of eggs inside a female fish.

clue.text: Done any prescription for a pain killer?

indicators.note: a prescription is something made up by a chemist, so these letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether any prescription has been issued for an analgesic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prescription' signals the anagram of DONEANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a medicine that soothes or relieves suffering.

clue.text: Kills ambitions

definitions.meaning: kills as a verb: finishes off, puts an end to
ambitions as nouns: goals or aims one works towards

explanation.definitionFit: To finish someone off is to end them; aims are the ends one pursues.

clue.text: Licensed everyone to marry, carrying ring

indicators.note: carrying means the first pieces hold another piece within them

parts.note: everyone means all
to marry means to wed
a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Everyone given permission to wed, provided they bring a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts O between ALL and WED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something licensed is permitted or authorised.

clue.text: Headland that continues to hide a monster

definitions.meaning: a promontory jutting into the sea, especially in Scottish place names

definitions.text: that continues to hide a monster
definitions.meaning: the Scottish loch said to conceal an elusive monster that nobody can find

explanation.surface: A promontory that still conceals some beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a coastal promontory; the loch of the same name supposedly hides its famous monster.

clue.text: Address of Riviera oafs on the move?

indicators.note: on the move says these letters shift about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking how clumsy louts on the French coast ought to be spoken to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a street location or a speech; here it means social skill. 'on the move' signals the anagram of RIVIERAOAFS.
explanation.definitionFit: Address in the sense of adroitness and tact is the social poise this French phrase describes.

clue.text: Support form of post that is slow to process

definitions.text: post that is slow to process

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a form at school is a class

explanation.surface: Backing for a kind of mail delivery that takes its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. The cheaper British postal service takes longer than first class.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheaper British mail tier is delivered more slowly than the premium service.

clue.text: Alarm facing the house

parts.note: the house is a theatre audience, and a performer before them can feel panic

explanation.surface: A fire alarm or burglar alarm positioned at the front of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' suggests a home; in the theatre it means the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous dread before performing to an audience is this performer's affliction.

clue.text: Practise art, possibly, that will make the flight more comfortable

definitions.text: that will make the flight more comfortable

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Advice to rehearse a craft that eases an aeroplane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel; it is a flight of steps. 'possibly' signals the anagram of PRACTISEART.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner of carpet fitted on steps softens the climb up a flight.

clue.text: Very first thing wrong in the garden?

definitions.text: Very first thing wrong in the garden?

parts.note: the very first is the original
a wrong deed is a sin

explanation.surface: Asking what the earliest misdeed in a garden was.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden is Eden, where Adam and Eve's disobedience was the first sin in Christian teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian doctrine holds that humanity inherits a sinful state from Adam's fall in Eden.

clue.text: Building society workers in pleasant scene

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words pleasant scene

explanation.surface: Bank staff from a mortgage lender pictured somewhere agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building society' looks like a British mortgage lender; read literally it is a colony of insects that builds a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker insects in a colony cooperatively build their nest.

clue.text: Prison disturbance

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for jail; also a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Developing acceptable condition of track at Epsom?

parts.note: something acceptable is on, as in 'that's not on'
the going is the state of the ground at a racecourse; Epsom is an English racecourse

explanation.surface: A racegoer's comment on suitable ground conditions as they change.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby; 'going' is racing's word for ground conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ongoing is continuing and in progress.

clue.text: Yielded to learner-driver, one that knocks down lots of people

definitions.text: one that knocks down lots of people

parts.note: yielded means gave
L is the plate a British learner driver displays

explanation.surface: Gave way to a novice motorist who then mowed down a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks down lots' is auction language: lots are sold with a tap of the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer's mallet is struck to signal each lot is sold.

clue.text: R1 at university?

definitions.meaning: the first of the three Rs taught in school: literacy, writing, arithmetic
a British student studies a subject, said as being at university for it

explanation.definitionFit: The first R of basic schooling; also the British verb for studying a subject at university.

clue.text: True male's sphere of action

parts.note: true means real

explanation.surface: A genuine man's field of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or field in which someone operates.

clue.text: Stopped losing head and relaxed

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: stopped means ceased

explanation.surface: Someone halted, lost their composure and then calmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes the C from CEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to loosen or become less tense.

clue.text: Neckwear that was uncomfortable, we are told

indicators.note: we are told says the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: uncomfortable can mean rough, as in a rough night

explanation.surface: A collar that apparently chafed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is a stiff pleated collar worn in Elizabethan times.

clue.text: Science article to look over

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A science feature for someone to read through.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan something is to survey or examine it.

clue.text: Gets undressed for slumber, when retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for slumber is read backwards

parts.note: slumber means sleep

explanation.surface: Someone takes their clothes off for a nap when going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like going to bed; it signals reversal, turning SLEEP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To peel off clothes is to strip.

clue.text: Imagine an old tribesman on the river

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Picture an ancient warrior on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to visualise it in the mind.

clue.text: European mining area in which lassie and I get involved

indicators.note: get involved means the letters are tangled up together into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl and the speaker get mixed up in a coalfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved' signals the anagram of LASSIEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia, a region of Poland and Czechia, is known for coal mining.

clue.text: A large drink called for a lady's maid

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: called here means spoken aloud, so the word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Someone orders a big drink for a woman's servant.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old term for a lady's maid, from a character in a 17th-century play.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically an abigail was a lady's personal attendant, after a waiting-woman in a Beaumont and Fletcher play.

clue.text: Manlier variety of soft drink

indicators.note: a variety of the word is another form of it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A more macho type of fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' signals the anagram of MANLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, mineral water and fizzy pop are both called minerals.

clue.text: Hindu demon taking in the sun?

definitions.text: Hindu demon taking in the sun?

parts.words: Hindu demon taking in the sun?
parts.note: in Hindu myth a severed demon's head swallows the sun, causing eclipses, not sunbathing

explanation.surface: A Hindu devil sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in the sun' suggests sunbathing; the demon literally swallows the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu mythology this demon's head devours the sun or moon, explaining eclipses.

clue.text: Appeal to advocate

definitions.meaning: appeal as a noun: an impulse or desire, or a request
to recommend or press for something

explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire or plea; also a verb meaning to press for something.

clue.text: Silly talk coming back from Hal burns

indicators.note: coming back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Nonsense coming back from someone called Hal, who is burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the hidden run HALB, which 'coming back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is meaningless or empty chatter.

clue.text: House common in home counties, next to motorway

indicators.note: next to says one piece is placed beside the other

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI here

explanation.surface: A type of house typical of suburbs around London, beside a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London; the M1 is a British motorway, with the 1 read as I. 'common in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a British semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Singular food fish

definitions.meaning: a flatfish eaten as food, such as the Dover variety

explanation.definitionFit: Means only or one alone; also a flatfish prized for the table.

clue.text: Pickles jar in place of unrest

parts.note: pickles as in tight spots or difficulties, troubles
a jar is a pot

explanation.surface: Pickled vegetables in a container somewhere turbulent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickles' looks like preserved food; it means predicaments.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouble spot is an area prone to conflict or violence.

clue.text: Cool flat set out

parts.note: flat means level
set out means headed off

explanation.surface: A calm apartment laid out neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' suggests an apartment; it means even.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool in the sense of calm and unflappable describes someone sensible and composed.
